title: Social Network OSINT
description: Learn how to investigate online identities, discover accounts, verify usernames, and use image-based search techniques using publicly available information.

sections.title: What is Social Network Intelligence?
sections.description: Social Network Intelligence involves using publicly available information from social platforms to build a better understanding of an online identity or target.
topics: Profile discovery and account finding
Username investigation across platforms
Social media research and analysis
Connecting information across different platforms
Cross-platform correlation of identities
sections.note: Our goal is NOT to break into accounts or bypass privacy. Our goal is to understand how much information can be discovered from legitimate public sources and how those pieces connect together.

sections.title: Challenges in Modern OSINT
sections.description: Social media platforms have introduced stronger privacy controls, better search systems, rate limits, and authentication requirements. Basic search queries are often not enough anymore.
topics: Meta platforms (Facebook, Instagram) only show publicly visible info
Private profiles cannot be accessed through normal search queries
Search engines have changed their indexing behavior
Many services restrict automated searches
Some information may exist in third-party or breach datasets — but not all is legally appropriate to access
sections.note: Focus only on legal and publicly accessible OSINT techniques. Never bypass privacy controls or access restrictions.

sections.title: Finding Users with Search Dorks
sections.description: Use search engine operators to find a specific person across platforms. This gives you more control than automated tools — you decide which platform to investigate and what to look for.

commands.description: Search for an exact name on Facebook. Replace Tom Johnson with your target name.

sections.title: Sherlock — Username Enumeration
sections.description: Sherlock automatically searches for a username across hundreds of websites. Useful for quickly generating potential leads — but results must always be manually verified.
sections.note: Sherlock results should NEVER be treated as confirmed evidence. The same username can belong to completely different people on different platforms. Automation finds leads — human analysis verifies them.

tools.description: Open-source username OSINT tool. Searches 300+ platforms automatically.

commands.description: Search for a username across 300+ platforms. Replace target_username with actual username.

sections.title: Method 1 — Target Synchronization
sections.description: Correlate different pieces of information associated with the same identity to determine whether they actually belong to the same person. Cross-reference usernames, aliases, and identifiers across public sources.
topics: Find a username on one public platform
Check if the same username appears on other public websites
Look for independent indicators: profile picture, bio, location, posting style
Compare writing style, interests, and linked accounts
Never force a private app to reveal identity or bypass authentication
sections.note: A matching username is a LEAD — not proof of identity. You need multiple independent indicators before making a strong attribution.

sections.title: Method 2 — Holehe (Email Investigation)
sections.description: Holehe is an open-source tool that checks whether an email address appears to be registered on various online services. An email address can be a powerful starting point for discovering a person's public digital footprint.
sections.note: An indication that an email exists on a service does NOT automatically prove ownership or identity. Treat it as an investigative lead and combine with other publicly available evidence.

sections.title: Reverse Image Search
sections.description: Find where a particular image appears online or discover visually similar images across publicly accessible sources. Useful for verifying profile pictures and discovering connected accounts.
sections.note: A facial image match is a LEAD, not proof of identity. Accuracy varies based on image quality, lighting, angle, and database coverage. Always manually verify using independent public sources.

commands.cmd: Workflow: Image → Upload to tool → Review results → Manual verification
commands.description: Always follow this workflow. Never skip the manual verification step.

sections.title: OSINT Verification Principles
sections.description: The most important part of Social Network OSINT is not finding information — it is verifying it. These principles apply to every investigation.
topics: Automation finds leads — human analysis verifies them
A matching username is a lead, not proof of identity
A facial match is a lead, not confirmed identity
An email match is a lead, not proof of ownership
Always look for multiple independent indicators before attribution
Compare: profile picture, bio, location, writing style, linked accounts, posting patterns
Document your findings and sources carefully
